results.evidenceText: Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship – Grants for Journalists Skip to content View Full List Grant details View all grants Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship Launched in 1949, the Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship seeks to promote the quality of responsible and discerning journalism exemplified by the work of Edward R. Murrow. One Edward R. Murrow Press fellowship is awarded each year to a distinguished foreign correspondent or editor to spend 10 months full time in residence at CFR’s headquarters in New York. The fellow is expected to engage in sustained analysis and writing, expand their intellectual and professional horizons, and contribute to CFR’s active program of research, writing, and events 🌍 Applicants must have a firm grounding in and a proposal based on foreign policy or a global issue. Location New York Funding Type Fellowship Organization Council on Foreign Relations Focus Area Subject Area International Affairs Award Size $100,000 plus a modest travel grant Career Stage Applicants must have distinguished credentials in the field of journalism that includes covering international news as a working journalist for print, broadcast, or online media widely available in the United States. Editor's Note Must be a U.S. citizen for this residency in New York City Deadline 10/30/2026 Apply Here

results.evidenceText: Morgan Stanley Sustainable Finance Fellowship Program 2027 (Paid) – Opportunity Desk Close Menu Home Conferences Training Scholarships Undergraduate Short Courses Online Courses Masters/Postgraduate PhD Postdoctoral Study Abroad Study in Africa Study in Asia Study in Australia Study in Europe Study in USA Competitions Awards Grants Fellowships Jobs Internships Volunteering Blog OD Specials OD Live Series Young Person of the Month Mentorship OD Mentors Success Stories How-To General Tips ODIC 2026 ODIC 2026 Application ODIC Judges ODIC 2025 Winners ODIC 2023 Winners ODIC 2022 Winners ODIC 2021 Winners ODIC 2019 Winners ODIC 2018 Winners ODIC 2017 Winners ODIC 2016 Winners Search Asia Africa Australia and Oceania America Europe Deadlines Approaching Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Monday, November 16 Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Instagram Telegram Morgan Stanley Sustainable Finance Fellowship Program 2027 (Paid) Jude Ogar October 30, 2026 3 Mins Read Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Pinterest LinkedIn Tumblr Email Telegram Deadline: November 13, 2026 Applications are invited for the Morgan Stanley Sustainable Finance Fellowship Program 2027 . The Sustainable Finance Summer Fellowship provides a unique opportunity to work with Morgan Stanley teams that seek to drive capital toward investments that promote sustainable economic growth and scalable solutions to global challenges. With support from across the Global Sustainability Office (GSO) and the Institute for Sustainable Investing, Morgan Stanley is dedicated to accelerating the adoption of sustainable investing, which seeks to deliver both competitive financial returns and positive environmental and social impact. GSO and the Institute partner across the Firm to pioneer scalable sustainable finance solutions, build new sustainable investing tools and generate industry-leading insights that inform and empower investors. The 10-week Sustainable Finance Summer Fellowship runs from early June to mid-August and places current graduate students on sustainability- or impact-focused teams at Morgan Stanley. Each Fellow will be assigned to a team based on their interests, skills and Firm needs. Past placement teams have included the Global Sustainability Office, Global Capital Markets (GCM), Private Credit & Equity (PC&E) and Wealth Management Investing with Impact (IIP). This program requires in-person attendance for the full 10 weeks in Morgan Stanley’s New York City offices. Responsibilities Fellowship projects will vary depending on which team a Fellow is placed with, but responsibilities may include: Conducting strategic business analysis and detailed industry research Building complex financial models Preparing and delivering presentations in a clear and compelling manner Monitoring and providing updates on market news Researching and analyzing emerging industry trends Gathering and analyzing data Contributing to and/or leading projects that support sustainable investing initiatives Benefits Expected base pay rate for the role will be $135,000 USD per year at the commencement of employment. However, base pay is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include discretionary bonuses and other Morgan Stanley-sponsored benefit programs. Eligibility Be currently working toward a master’s degree or enrolled in a graduate-level program; Possess a clear and demonstrable interest in sustainability and finance; Be able to summarize and articulate complex ideas effectively; Be a team player and a self-starter who enjoys working on projects independently and in groups; Possess strong organizational skills and the ability to work under tight deadlines; Manage multiple projects and stakeholders efficiently. Application Submit a resume and, separately, answer the following question in no more than 300 words: What is one sustainability issue or theme that you believe deserves greater attention from investors, businesses or policymakers? Why do you think it is often overlooked, and what are the consequences if it continues to receive insufficient attention? Click here to apply For more information, visit Morgan Stanley Sustainable Finance Fellowship . Share. results.evidenceText: Call for Mentees: Telemachus & Athena Mentoring Programme 2027 – Opportunity Desk Close Menu Home Conferences Training Scholarships Undergraduate Short Courses Online Courses Masters/Postgraduate PhD Postdoctoral Study Abroad Study in Africa Study in Asia Study in Australia Study in Europe Study in USA Competitions Awards Grants Fellowships Jobs Internships Volunteering Blog OD Specials OD Live Series Young Person of the Month Mentorship OD Mentors Success Stories How-To General Tips ODIC 2026 ODIC 2026 Application ODIC Judges ODIC 2025 Winners ODIC 2023 Winners ODIC 2022 Winners ODIC 2021 Winners ODIC 2019 Winners ODIC 2018 Winners ODIC 2017 Winners ODIC 2016 Winners Search Asia Africa Australia and Oceania America Europe Deadlines Approaching Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Monday, November 16 Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Instagram Telegram Call for Mentees: Telemachus & Athena Mentoring Programme 2027 Jude Ogar October 30, 2026 2 Mins Read Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Pinterest LinkedIn Tumblr Email Telegram Deadline: November 23, 2026 Applications are open for mentees to join the Telemachus & Athena Mentoring Programme 2027 . The mentoring programmes ‘Telemachus’ and ‘Athena’ connect mentees with thought leaders and social-impact focused individuals. Telemachus benefits youth between 18-29 from around the world, while Athena focuses on women above the age of 22 and without setting an age limit. Global Thinkers Forum (GTF) mentees are provided with a personalized development opportunity to address individual learning needs. This opportunity helps them over a period of eight months to develop new skills and expertise, and to enhance, enrich and expand their professional and personal perspectives. Benefits Upon successful completion of the cycle, you will have gained valuable insights for your career, new perspectives and new skills. Moreover, you will most probably have gained a lifelong friend! You will receive a programme completion certificate and you will become part of the broader GTF community which will be a network of support to you. You will also earn an optional 3-month internship with GTF. Eligibility You are eligible to apply for ‘Telemachus’ if you are a young individual between 18-29. ‘Athena’ is for women above the age of 22 and without age limit. If you fall in the categories, feel free to apply. Applicants with fluent command of English, who have completed a Bachelor’s degree or have equally-relevant professional experience of a minimum of 5 years will be prioritised. Application Click here to apply For more information, visit Telemachus & Athena Mentoring Programme . Share. results.pageTitle: Fault Lines Reporting Fund - GFMD
results.pageDescription: The IWMF's Fault Lines Reporting Fund supports journalists reporting on the forces driving racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, misogyny, and other forms of intolerance promoting hate in the United States.
results.evidenceText: Fault Lines Reporting Fund - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Fault Lines Reporting Fund Organisation: International Women’s Media Foundation Status: Open Type: Grant Theme: Freedom of expression Funding Size: USD 2,500–USD 10,000 Deadline: Ongoing Eligibility: USA journalists writing about discrimination Target Region: USA Application Language: English The IWMF’s Fault Lines Reporting Fund supports journalists reporting on the forces driving racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, misogyny, and other forms of intolerance promoting hate in the United States. Successful applications examine how false, divisive, and harmful narratives — such as stories that promote or normalise hate, discrimination, and the dehumanisation of individuals and communities — take hold, including what is fuelling them, where they are most pronounced, the scope of their impact, and where individuals and communities are making real progress in combating these hate-based agendas. The three-year programme provides grants to staff and freelance journalists planning well-researched, investigative, and evidence-based reporting within the United States. Grant funds may be used to cover travel, logistics, security, insurance, and other reporting-related expenses. Eligibility Applicants must report in the United States. The applicant’s primary profession must be journalism; applications will be accepted from freelance, staff, or content-based journalists. Applicants must have 3+ years of professional journalism experience outside of internships. Applicants must present a strong track record of exceptional journalism or show proof of interest from an editor. Requirements A completed application in English (reporting itself may be conducted in any language). A well-developed story pitch demonstrating investigative merit, originality, reach, potential impact, and need for funding. Supporting documentation demonstrating journalistic track record. Grantees must publish in a U.S. outlet within one year of receiving a grant and must credit the IWMF. How to Apply Submit the application through the IWMF Submittable portal on a rolling basis; there is no fixed closing date for the current programme cycle. Larger awards are considered on a case-by-case basis. Apply here . For more information, please visit this page . results.title: the equality fund global journalism fellowship 2026
results.pageTitle: the Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026 - GFMD
results.pageDescription: The Equality Fund, a global fund investing in people with local solutions to global challenges, is launching its inaugural Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship. Journalists in ODA-recipient countries are invited to apply now through November 8, 2026 at 11pm, Eastern Standard Time.
results.evidenceText: the Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026 - GFMD « Back to all Fundings the Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026 Organisation: Equality Fund Status: Closed Type: Fellowship Theme: Media support Funding Size: $4,000 Deadline: 08/11/2026 Eligibility: Journalists in ODA-recipient countries Target region: ODA countries ( see here ) Application language: English (reporting can be any language) The Equality Fund, a global fund investing in people with local solutions to global challenges, is launching its inaugural Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship. Journalists in ODA-recipient countries are invited to apply now through November 8, 2026 at 11pm, Eastern Standard Time. Requirements The Equality Fund welcomes journalism across a range of formats, including written articles, audio, video, and other digital storytelling formats, as long as the project is grounded in fact-based reporting with a clear editorial purpose. Podcast episodes or audio projects are eligible if they include original reporting and interviews. Informal conversations are not a fit, but long-form interviews, reported audio features, and documentary-style episodes are eligible. Social media storytelling is eligible if the format is used to tell a reported, journalistic story. The Equality Fund is open to digital-first and non-traditional formats, including video and social media storytelling, as long as the work is grounded in reporting and verification. Your story should not be finished. It should be in a proposal state. If you have already reported on this community or issue or theme in the past, that’s great. But the story itself cannot already be produced. You will be in community with the other fellows as you all work through story pitch to reporting to publication phases. The Equality Fund uses journalism to mean work that involves original reporting, fact-checking, and publication through a recognized outlet or platform involving more than one person. They recognize that some applicants may not describe themselves as journalists, especially freelancers or independent creators, but may still be doing journalistic work. Eligibility Minimum of three years of journalism experience Journalists should be located in, and be reporting on, communities in ODA-recipient countries Have three strong journalism samples that showcase a range of relevant work Ability to accommodate meetings within daytime hours in Eastern Standard Time Fluent in English, Equality Fund’s working language Have a strong affinity for Equality Fund’s mission, and align with their values – equality and diversity of race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, national origin, and disability Women, non-binary, and trans people are encouraged to apply Have an account with a bank that is able to accept international Electronic Wire Transfers How to apply Closing Date for applications is November 8, 2026 at midnight, Eastern Standard Time. Applications sent outside of the form will not be considered. Incomplete applications (applications not containing a sample of work, letter of motivation, and CV) will not be considered. Successful applicants will be contacted by January 15, 2027. Apply here . For more information, please visit this page . results.title: lmdif western balkans fund
results.pageTitle: LMDIF Western Balkans Fund - GFMD
results.pageDescription: MDIF Western Balkans Fund is a strategic initiative to foster growth and resilience in independent media in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia.
results.evidenceText: LMDIF Western Balkans Fund - GFMD « Back to all Fundings LMDIF Western Balkans Fund Organisation: Media Development Investment Fund (MDIF) Status: Open Type: Equity Investments Theme: Democracy and good governance Funding Size: N/A Deadline: Ongoing Eligibility: Media located in or serving audiences in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. Target Region: Balkans Application Language: English MDIF Western Balkans Fund is a strategic initiative to foster growth and resilience in independent media in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. It takes a holistic investment approach, utilizing a versatile strategy of loans, equity and quasi-equity supported by media business expertise. The Fund focuses investments on innovative start-ups, growth media undergoing digital transformation and protecting independent media from capture. The Fund seeks to bridge the financing gap that often hinders growth, and supports the development of robust, financially and editorially independent media companies that are able to support the advancement of their societies. Eligibility Applicants must demonstrate dedication to providing unique, credible and independent news in the public interest within the Western Balkans. Applicants must actively contribute to addressing issues of accountability and strengthening public debate in the region. Applicants must uphold principles of transparency, human rights and equal rights for all, irrespective of race, ethnicity, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, religion and other subjects of discrimination. Ownership must be independent of government or any other political or economic interests. Applicants must be located in or serving audiences in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. Requirements The Fund catalyses capital, mobilizing financing to empower independent media enterprises in the region through no-strings-attached financing that drives growth and protects independen The amount MDIF invests in each company is dependent on many factors, including the stage of company development and the total round-size and location. When applying, please provide the total amount of money you are raising and how much of the round has already been raised (if any). MDIF’s media expertise and more than two decades of working in the Western Balkans give the Fund a unique approach. MDIF’s experience and networks ensure quality deal flow, and mission-screening by their Board of Directors ensures alignment with the fund’s mission objectives. How to apply You can send in your application to gro.fidm@fbw. If you have a question that isn’t answered on the website, please contact gro.fidm@fbw. For more information, please visit this page . The MIT Summer Research Program (MSRP) is a competitive summer initiative designed to promote the value of graduate education, broaden participation in the research enterprise, and prepare and recruit exceptional undergraduate students for graduate study at MIT and beyond. Launched in 1986, the MIT Summer Research Program (MSRP) was created to expand access to research opportunities for students whose educational journeys and experiences have not always aligned with traditional pathways into graduate education. The program continues to foster a more inclusive academic environment by supporting students with diverse life experiences, academic interests, and educational backgrounds. MSRP seeks to identify talented undergraduates who might benefit from spending a summer on MIT’s campus, conducting research under the guidance of MIT faculty members, postdoctoral fellows, and advanced graduate students. Students who participate in this program will be better prepared and motivated to pursue advanced degrees, thereby helping to sustain a rich talent pool in critical areas of research and innovation. Benefits Mentored Research Experience: Work under the guidance of an MIT faculty member, with additional support from a postdoctoral fellow or advanced graduate student. Graduate School Preparation: Receive individualized advising on academic and research career pathways, including feedback on coursework and lab skill development. Scholarly Engagement: Gain the opportunity to contribute to publishable research and potentially co-author a scientific paper with your faculty mentor. Cutting-Edge Facilities: Conduct research in state-of-the-art laboratories across MIT departments and interdisciplinary centers. Financial Support: Weekly stipend, round-trip travel to MIT, meal subsidy, and housing are provided. Campus Access: Enjoy access to MIT’s libraries, athletic facilities, and health services. Eligibility Applicants must: Have a minimum 3.5 overall or major GPA (on a 4.0 scale). Be enrolled full-time in a degree-granting program at a U.S. institution of higher education located in the U.S. or its territories (excluding MIT). Be a sophomore, junior, or non-graduating senior with at least two academic years of college coursework completed (excluding college credit earned during high school or its equivalent). Students should not be graduating prior to December 2027. Note: First-year students from select undergraduate institutions may be eligible to apply through the Leadership Alliance’s James H. Wyche First Year Research Program (FYRE). Have an interest in pursuing a graduate degree in one of MIT’s graduate programs, Sloan professional programs not included (MBA, EMBA, LGO, etc). Have a genuine interest in pursuing a career in academic research and/or teaching. Be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, non-U.S. citizen with DACA, or international student with appropriate visa and work authorizations. Application All application materials must be submitted by this deadline. Applications submitted after 11:59 PM ET on January 19 will not be accepted. This includes all required documents and letters of recommendation, no exceptions. Click here to apply For more information, visit MIT Summer Research Program . Share. results.pageDescription: Retraction Watch and The Open Notebook are thrilled to introduce the first two fellows in our Research Accountability Reporting Fellowship. This program, supported by The Center for Scientific Integrity, equips journalists at local newsrooms to cover issues of scientific integrity, such as misconduct, data manipulation, fraud, and problematic publishing.
results.evidenceText: Announcing the First Research Accountability Reporting Fellows—and a New Slate of Trainings! - The Open Notebook Skip to content News & Announcements Announcing the First Research Accountability Reporting Fellows—and a New Slate of Trainings! TON Editors September 28, 2026 Retraction Watch and The Open Notebook are thrilled to introduce the first two fellows in our Research Accountability Reporting Fellowship . This program, supported by The Center for Scientific Integrity , equips journalists at local newsrooms to cover issues of scientific integrity, such as misconduct, data manipulation, fraud, and problematic publishing. Local journalists are uniquely positioned to hold scientific institutions in their coverage areas to account. Investigating wrongdoing in science mirrors traditional investigative work—with a few added skills. Retraction Watch and The Open Notebook have joined forces to train journalists to add research accountability reporting to their repertoire. As part of this program, we are also offering three free, virtual trainings designed to introduce research accountability reporting as an investigative skill any journalist can hone. Prospective applicants for the reporting fellowship and anyone interested in learning this skill is welcome to attend. Introducing the Inaugural Research Accountability Reporting Fellows This six-month fellowship program provides journalists at local newsrooms with one-to-one mentoring support as they investigate a scientific integrity issue centered on research institutions in their region. Newsrooms working with selected fellows will also receive $7,500 to support their reporting project. We are still taking applications and awarding fellowships on a rolling basis. Courtesy of Kayla Yup Kayla Yup is a health reporter at the Philadelphia Inquirer , with bylines in the Wall Street Journal , In These Times , The Nation , The Nation’s Health , and The Blade in Toledo, Ohio. She was previously a fellow with the Investigative Reporting Lab at Yale. Kayla’s editor at the Inquirer is Letitia Stein, and her mentor for the fellowship is Retraction Watch co-founder Adam Marcus. Angelica Edwards / The Assembly Matt Hartman is a higher education reporter at The Assembly . A longtime freelance journalist who has written for The New Republic , The Ringer , Jacobin , and elsewhere, he also spent nearly a decade working in higher ed communications. Matt’s editor at The Assembly is Emily Stephenson, and his mentors for the fellowship are Retraction Watch co-founder Ivan Oransky and managing editor Kate Travis. Register for Our Research Accountability Reporting Trainings Join the new fellows and instructors from Retraction Watch and The Open Notebook for a series of trainings on how to do research accountability reporting. These trainings are free for anyone to attend. REGISTER HERE What is Accountability Journalism in Science and Why Does It Matter? Monday, October 5 at 1:00 p.m. ET The scientific process is designed to be rigorous and objective, but it’s also an industry with faults and broken systems. Learn how scientific publishing works, including how financial incentives, pressure to publish, and lacking federal regulation can create a ripe environment for misconduct. Digging into Accountability Stories Tuesday, October 20 at 2:00 p.m. ET You get a tip about a researcher manipulating data or you come across a string of retracted papers—now what? Learn how to sniff out an accountability story and what steps to take early in the investigative process. We’ll talk through the online tools databases, and trusted experts available to journalists reporting on scientific integrity. Anatomy of an Accountability Reporting Project: Following an Investigation from Start to Finish Monday, November 2 at 1:00 p.m. ET Like any investigative project, research accountability stories can quickly become a tangled web of conflicting reports, public records requests, and elusive sources. Learn how to keep your reporting organized and what to do when you run into obstacles. We’ll also cover best practices for publishing ironclad investigative projects and how to handle harassment. During this training, this year’s fellows will share lessons learned from their own projects. Interested in Applying for the Fellowship? Applications are still open for this fellowship. Up to four more fellowships will be awarded on a rolling basis. Any U.S.-based local or regional journalist working on staff or freelancing for a media outlet that has a research university or institution in their coverage area is invited to apply. Participating newsrooms will receive the fellowship stipend to support the fellows’ proposed reporting projects. Applicants must provide a letter of support from a staff editor at the outlet they work for or contract with. LEARN MORE Questions? Please email [email protected] with questions about the fellowship program or upcoming trainings. Thanks for reading! If you found this useful, sign up for our e-mail newsletter , take a free course , or support our work . Gregory Barber on Covering Climate Models Rohini Subrahmanyam Skip to content
